text:
Alice (support): hey team, seeing multiple customer escalations since ~02:45 UTC about 401s: 'invalid_signature' and a bunch of 'kid mismatch' errors. affected tenant: tenant-47-prod. grabbing logs now :eyes:

Ben (eng-infra): can you paste an example error blob? stack traces or exact auth log lines help.

Alice (support): pasted below, redacted token ids:
```
[2026-03-15T02:46:12Z] tenant=tenant-47 request_id=abc123 auth=fail reason=invalid_signature token.kid=old-key-2023 verifier_kids=[new-key-2025]
[2026-03-15T02:46:12Z] stack=auth.verify: signature verification failed (kid mismatch)
```

Carlos (sre): hmmm. kid mismatch usually means the client's token references a key we don't currently have in our JWKS cache. did tenant-47 recently rotate keys on their IdP?

Alice (support): customer says they did a planned rotation at 02:40UTC and confirmed tokens issued with kid='old-key-2023' for a short overlap window. our JWKS endpoint cached the new keys and removed the old key too quickly? they saw ~30-40% of requests fail.

Dana (auth): timeline theory: their IdP rotated keys, published a new JWKS entry (new-key-2025), then removed old key earlier than they expected. But we should support transient overlap: we cache JWKS and respect cache headers, but also have to handle revalidation and ETag/304 logic. can you curl the jwks URL we used?

Alice (support): did a quick fetch:
```
$ curl -i https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nCache-Control: max-age=300, public\nETag: "v2026-03-15-02:44"\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{"keys":[{"kid":"new-key-2025","kty":"RSA","n":"...","e":"AQAB"}]}
```

Carlos (sre): there it is — no old-key returned. but why earlier logs show verifier_kids=[new-key-2025] while token.kid=old-key-2023 — that explains signature failure. two possibilities: 1) client token has older kid (rotation overlap) but IdP already removed old key (so tokens truly unverifiable), or 2) our JWKS cache logic performed a revalidation that returned 304 and we incorrectly replaced the cache body with an empty result or dropped stale keys.

Ben (eng-infra): do we log JWKS fetch/responses? I want to see whether we got a 304 from origin.

deploy-bot: JWKS refresh job for tenant-47 ran at 2026-03-15T02:44:50Z -> GET /.well-known/jwks.json -> HTTP 304 Not Modified (ETag: "v2026-03-15-02:30") ; cache ttl remaining: 0s; replaced cache: true

Dana (auth): deploy-bot log suggests our JWKS worker used conditional GET and got 304, then 'replaced cache: true' looks suspicious. 304 should mean 'not modified' -> keep existing cache, not replace with empty body. if our code path interpreted 304 as 'fresh but empty' it could have cleared keys. that would cause kid mismatch for any tokens that relied on keys previously seen.

Ben (eng-infra): filing a quick debug PR to add stricter handling and more logging around 304. immediate mitigation: rehydrate JWKS from backup cache when verification fails and token.kid present. also add metric jwks.fetch.304_count and jwks.cache.replacements to track.

Alice (support): customer is asking for a short-term mitigation. can we patch runner to attempt a forced JWKS refresh on 401 invalid_signature if token.kid not found? fallback flow suggestion:
1) verify token -> kid not found -> force GET jwks?cache_bust=1 -> if new key present, retry verification -> else return 401 and include header X-Auth-Diagnostics: kid-missing,fetch-attempted

Dana (auth): agree. low-risk. implement gated rollout for Dedicated and Hosted. also add TTL min of 30s and max of 5m, unless origin Cache-Control smaller. we should never clear cache on 304. fix in 2-step: quick patch to change 304 handling (hotfix), then follow-up to add forced-refresh-on-missing-kid.

Carlos (sre): also consider clock skew: we saw a few 'jwt expired' errors from tenant-47 around same time. their tokens had iat/exp very tight (30s validity) and their clock was ~40s behind our servers. recommend we accept up to +-60s skew for verification(clock_tolerance configurable per-tenant). add metric auth.clock_skew_rejections.

Ben (eng-infra): created ticket INFRA-8723 with repro steps and proposed changes. repro steps attached:
```
1) generate token with KID=old-key-2023 (simulate rotated token)
2) remove old-key from jwks.json and publish new-key only
3) configure our runtime to fetch jwks (with ETag/If-None-Match) and simulate 304 handling path
4) observe verify failures when cache accidentally cleared
```

Alice (support): customer wants a postmortem and a temporary whitelist for tenant-47. can we add a one-off policy to trust tokens signed by _either_ key if they present a specific header or client cert? risk: accepting unknown keys is dangerous. alternative: support replay of tokens to their IdP introspection endpoint for acceptance during rotation window. thoughts?

Dana (auth): don't accept arbitrary keys. safer: enable token introspection fallback for that tenant for the next 2 hours and keep detailed audit logs. ask customer to enable introspection on their IdP for the rollout window. I'll draft an email template.

Carlos (sre): action items: 
- Dana: hotfix for 304 handling and add forced JWKS refresh on missing kid (canary 10% -> 50% -> all) (ETA 2h)
- Ben: add metrics and INFRA-8723 details + repro scripts (ETA 1h)
- Alice: coordinate customer comms + enable introspection fallback if they opt-in (ETA 30m)
- Carlos: add auth.clock_tolerance config and metric (PR after hotfix)

Alice (support): thanks. I'll update tenant-47 and tell them we have a hotfix rolling and a fallback plan. updating support ticket now and will attach logs and suggested IdP steps. :thumbsup:

Ben (eng-infra): quick note — once hotfix merged, we should run a synthetic rotation test for all tenants with scheduled key rotations next week. add to runbook.

Dana (auth): agreed. also add a unit/integration test that simulates 304 and ensures cache isn't replaced.

Alice (support): I'll close initial support escalation after customer's confirmation. will reopen if anything else pops. thanks everyone.
